page: Microsoft Azure D32plds_v7 is an ARM-based virtual machine configuration within the general purpose Dpldsv7 series, provisioned on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs operating on the 64-bit ARM architecture (arm64) paired with 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. Graphical processing units are not included in this configuration.

A key component of this virtual machine is the inclusion of 1890 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. The local solid-state drive provides low-latency temporary storage capacity directly attached to the host, facilitating data-intensive tasks that require swift read and write cycles without relying purely on remote disks.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU distribution places the instance into a compute-dense profile relative to standard 1:4 memory configurations. This resource allocation offers cost efficiency for applications that prioritize execution parallelism and raw compute capacity over expansive system memory per core. However, memory-bound workloads or environments requiring x86-specific instruction sets may encounter limitations due to the 2.0 GB per core ceiling and the arm64 platform requirements.

Given its high core count, low memory footprint per thread, and fast integrated NVMe storage, the instance fits tasks such as application build pipelines, scale-out web serving, caching tiers, data preprocessing pipelines, batch computing, and scratchpad-heavy database workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure D32plds_v7 is an ARM-based virtual machine in the Dpldsv7 series designed for compute-intensive general purpose workloads. Operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the server provides 32 dedicated 64-bit ARM vCPUs paired with 64.0 GB of system RAM, resulting in a 2.0 GB per vCPU density. It bundles a high-capacity 1890 GB local NVMe SSD to support low-latency temporary I/O operations and features Premium Storage compatibility, with zero GPU hardware included. The 1:2 core-to-memory ratio provides economical compute efficiency for applications that do not demand extensive RAM footprint per thread. This instance configuration is tailored for workloads such as continuous integration and build agents, batch processing, scale-out web applications, caching systems, and high-throughput temporary storage tasks that can execute natively on arm64 architecture.
